key_insight: A 3D CNN can learn surrogate models for subgrid turbulent transport in quiet-Sun simulations and reconstruct Reynolds stress tensor components more accurately than classical baselines.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven alternative for improving coarse-grid solar plasma simulations where unresolved turbulence strongly affects momentum transport and energy dissipation.
method: Train a 3D convolutional neural network on 3D velocity fields to capture spatial dependencies.
Augment inputs with velocity components and scalar plasma density features.
Compare against an MLP and physics-based Gradient and Smagorinsky models, and test logarithmic target transforms for skewed stress data.
evidence_signal: The final 3DCNN reportedly improves average accuracy by about 31% on diagonal Reynolds stress components and about 8% on off-diagonal components versus baselines.
watch_item: Generalization may be limited by the specific simulation regime and by sensitivity to target scaling/log transforms, so deployment should be validated on new solar conditions and resolutions.
paper_title: Developing Machine Learning Models of Subgrid Turbulent Transport for Quiet Sun 3D Radiative Hydrodynamic Simulations
